knowledge:
- key_parameters: path=The directory location where the FASTQ files of interest are saved ;; pattern=A regular expression (e.g., ".fastq.gz") to identify target files in the directory ;; n=Number of records to sample from each FASTQ file (default is 1 million) ;; sample=Logical value; if FALSE, the file is processed as a whole instead of sampling records ;; workers=Number of cores/workers for parallel processing (interfacing with BiocParallel); set workers=1 for serial processing ;; outdir=Directory where the generated HTML report will be written ;; templateFile=Path to a custom R Markdown template file for personalized reports
- alternatives: ShortRead package (specifically the .QA class, which RqcResultSet extends)
- when_to_use: When performing initial quality control and assessment of high-throughput sequencing data (FASTQ files) to check read quality, GC content, read length distribution, and base call proportions
- pitfalls: By default, rqc samples 1 million records (sample=TRUE); if the user wants to process the entire file, they must explicitly set sample=FALSE ;; rqcFileHeatmap only works with one result file (and not a list/multiple files)

workflows.name: simple_qc_report
workflows.intent: Quickly generate an HTML quality control report from a directory of FASTQ files.
input: folder (path to directory containing FASTQ files)
pattern (regular expression to match FASTQ files, e.g., ".fastq.gz")
workflows.stages: 1. Load the package ;; 2. Define the input directory ;; 3. Run the rqc function to process files and generate the HTML report.
workflows.code:
library(Rqc)
folder <- system.file(package="ShortRead", "extdata/E-MTAB-1147")
rqc(path = folder, pattern = ".fastq.gz")

workflows.name: advanced_qc_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform step-by-step quality control analysis, generate individual diagnostic plots, and compile a customized HTML report.
input: files (vector of absolute paths to FASTQ files)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the package ;; 2. Define the vector of input file paths ;; 3. Process files using rqcQA to generate an RqcResultSet object ;; 4. Generate individual diagnostic plots (e.g., quality boxplots, average quality, GC content, base calls) ;; 5. Extract processed data for custom plotting using rqcCycleAverageQualityCalc ;; 6. Generate the HTML report using rqcReport.
workflows.code:
library(Rqc)
fastqDir <- system.file(package="ShortRead", "extdata/E-MTAB-1147")
files <- list.files(fastqDir, "fastq.gz", full.names=TRUE)
qa <- rqcQA(files, workers=1)
knitr::kable(perFileInformation(qa))
rqcReadQualityBoxPlot(qa)
rqcReadQualityPlot(qa)
rqcCycleAverageQualityPlot(qa)
rqcReadFrequencyPlot(qa)
rqcFileHeatmap(qa[[1]])
rqcReadWidthPlot(qa)
rqcCycleGCPlot(qa)
rqcCycleQualityPlot(qa)
rqcCycleAverageQualityPcaPlot(qa)
rqcCycleQualityBoxPlot(qa)
rqcCycleBaseCallsPlot(qa)
rqcCycleBaseCallsLinePlot(qa)
df <- rqcCycleAverageQualityCalc(qa)
cycle <- as.numeric(levels(df$cycle))[df$cycle]
plot(cycle, df$quality, col = df$filename, xlab='Cycle', ylab='Quality Score')
sublist <- qa[1]
rqcCycleQualityPlot(sublist)
reportFile <- rqcReport(qa)
browseURL(reportFile)
rqcReport(qa, templateFile = "custom_report.Rmd")
